findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has no topic_users row for this topic (for example, opening the emailed link in a different browser/session where no row was ever created, or after the row was removed). Line 107 immediately calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row when missing) or otherwise handle the nil case.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by a plain GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe action is routed as GET (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and mutates notification_level on every request. Email link scanners, antivirus prefetchers, browser prefetch, and simply reloading the page will therefore change the user's notification state without any intentional confirmation click. A mail security gateway that follows links can silently mute topics for users who never clicked anything.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent and does not actually mute on first click
findings.body: Each visit steps the level down exactly one notch: watching/tracking becomes regular, and only a second visit (or a refresh of the landing page) becomes muted. So the first click on the email link leaves the user at regular — still notified of mentions/quotes/replies to their posts — while the landing page claims 'You will stop receiving notifications', and a refresh unexpectedly changes state again. The action should set a single deterministic target level (muted) in one idempotent operation.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: Mutating tu.notification_level and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the canonical path used by set_notifications: it stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message, and runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for. As written, already-open clients keep showing the old notification level and downstream observers/audit data are never updated.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every unsubscribe email
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string for any message built with add_unsubscribe_link: true. Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url; any other current or future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to deliver mail entirely, instead of simply omitting the per-topic sentence. The per-topic line should be conditional on unsubscribe_url being present.

findings.title: Ember route/controller/template names for unsubscribe do not match
findings.body: The route is registered as top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' (with controller controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 and view views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, i.e. topic-unsubscribe), but the template is placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Ember's resolver will look for a topic-unsubscribe template for this route and find none, so the unsubscribe landing page renders empty/without the notification-state controls even though the server-side mutation already happened.

findings.title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behavior end-to-end
findings.body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing fixture but adds no assertion that the per-topic URL appears in the body/HTML, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (missing TopicUser row, watching vs regular vs muted starting levels, slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The nil-row crash and the one-notch-at-a-time behavior above would both have been caught by such specs.
